newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: VNU, CHRYSALIS IN TV VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: VNU, CHRYSALIS IN TV VENTURE.

text.p: Dutch publisher NV Verenigd Bezit VNU said on Friday it would set a jointly-owned television production company with Chrysalis Group Plc.
VNU said the group would include IDTV, the Netherlands' second largest television production company.
The venture will be called CVI Media Group and will be 50.1 percent owned by Chrysalis with VNU holding the remaining 49.9.
IDTV was formerly 49 percent owned by Chrysalis, which will swap the stake for its new holding in CVI. The other 51 percent of IDTV was sold to CVI by its founder Harry de Winter.
VNU will pay 51.3 million guilders for its 49.9 percent stake in CVI Media Group, it said, adding decision making within the group would be equally divided.

VNU said it would pay a additional sum in 1999 which will depend on IDTV's profitability in the coming three years. It added it would also supply CVI Media Group with an unspecified credit facitility.
IDTV was set up in 1979 and entered an alliance with Chysalis in 1994. The company posted 1995 net profits of 4.7 million guilders on turnover of 60 million.
The company will be continued unter the management of Harry de Winter, who will also become chief executive of CVI Media.
The deal, which is aimed at enabling further TV expansion in Europe, is expected to be finalised by the end of the year.
The news of the venture comes within hours of the flotation of Dutch television production company Endemol Entertainment on the Amsterdam bourse.

Shares in Endemol, which is market leader in the Dutch television production field with 1995/96 sales of 642.4 million guilders, were floated at 48 guilders on Friday and within hours were trading nearly 10 higher at 57.50.
